loggia_thermal_consequence.finding: !! THE ЛОДЖИЯ IS THERMALLY DECOUPLED FROM THE FLAT, AND THAT CUTS AGAINST THE OWNER'S OWN GOAL.
reasoning: The wall between the flat and the лоджия - M1, plus M7 and the insulated face of R8 - is full warm perimeter: 300 mm block with 70 mm of mineral wool.
So essentially NO heat leaks from the heated flat into the лоджия. One might otherwise have assumed some did.
M2 separates this лоджия from the neighbour's, and both are unheated - cold-to-cold, no help from that side either.
The лоджия's own enclosure is thin and uninsulated by design: M2 'thinner', M6b ~200 mm provisional.
The floor and ceiling are slabs shared with the loggias above and below, which are also unheated.
loggia_thermal_consequence.consequence: !! THE STANDING TARGET - keep the лоджия frost-free through an ordinary Belarusian winter with NO heating, on passive measures alone - therefore rests on exactly two things: SOLAR GAIN, and the лоджия's OWN enclosure. Nothing is contributed by the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_good_news: Solar gain is the best it could be: the лоджия's main angled glazing faces DUE SOUTH (confirmed orientation), making it the most solar-exposed element in the flat.
loggia_thermal_consequence.the_work: So the glazing upgrade the owner is already planning is doing nearly all of the work, and the thin uninsulated enclosure walls (M2, M6b) are the weak points. Whether the target is achievable at all is an open question the vault has already flagged as a content gap - see 00_Master/Family_Requirements.md section 10 - and this is the constraint set that question has to be answered against.
loggia_thermal_consequence.note_on_scope: The owner has decided NOT to join the лоджия to the flat and to keep its doors and windows. That decision is unaffected; what changes is where the heat has to come from.

thin_70mm.note: Seven regions, all on the aerated-block external walls.

insulation_is_NOT_uniform_2026_09_04.why_it_explains_itself: !! CONCRETE CONDUCTS HEAT FAR BETTER THAN AERATED BLOCK, so an exposed frame element is a THERMAL BRIDGE and needs more insulation to compensate. 150 on concrete, 70 on block is exactly the pattern he marked - so the marking is internally coherent and does not need to be taken on trust.
insulation_is_NOT_uniform_2026_09_04.consequence_for_the_loggia: !! R8 IS THE FLAT/ЛОДЖИЯ WALL AND IT CARRIES THE THICKER 150. So even less heat reaches the лоджия than the earlier finding assumed - the frost-free-without-heating target rests on solar gain and the лоджия own enclosure, and essentially nothing else. This strengthens that finding rather than changing it.
insulation_is_NOT_uniform_2026_09_04.consequence_for_heat_loss: Any heat-loss calculation must use 150 mm over R8/R9 and 70 mm over the M-series, not a single figure. The thermal-bridge treatment is already designed in, which is a point in the building favour.

frame_thickness_derived.how: !! DERIVED FROM THE PLAN ITSELF, not asked: the plan prints 175 at each place a column meets a partition, and 250 - 75 = 175. The printed step only works arithmetically if the frame is 250 AND the partitions are 75, so it corroborates both at once - a stronger check than either figure alone.

general_thickness_rules_2026_09_04.source: Owner, stated as general rules rather than wall by wall.
rules: 1. Every INTERNAL wall on the flat's outer perimeter - to an adjacent flat, or to another area inside the building such as the common corridor - is 250 mm. Applies to G2, G3, G5, G4a.
2. All OUTER walls are 300 mm plus 70 mm insulation. Applies to M1, M3, M4, M5, M6a, M7.
3. CONCRETE walls are 250 mm, and where exposed they carry 150 mm insulation. Applies to R1a-R9, with the 150 on R8 and R9.
4. M2 is 200 mm aerated block with NO insulation - the divider to the adjacent лоджия.
general_thickness_rules_2026_09_04.resolves: !! G5 = 250 by rule 1, which CLOSES the 200-or-250 question. That was the last figure able to move the living room wall line, and therefore the Phase-2 combined zone.
general_thickness_rules_2026_09_04.state: THE THICKNESS MODEL IS NOW COMPLETE for all 30 block runs. Only two figures are not directly from the owner: G1 at 120 (inferred from the plan) and M6b at 200 (his own provisional revision, pending another plan).

insulation_follows_the_facade_not_the_en.finding: !! M6b IS insulated at 70 even though the лоджия is unheated, while M2 is explicitly NOT insulated. The difference is not thermal.
insulation_follows_the_facade_not_the_en.explanation: M6b is ON THE VISIBLE, RENDERED FAÇADE; M2 faces another лоджия and is never seen from outside. So the insulation follows the RENDERED FAÇADE PLANE, not the thermal envelope.
insulation_follows_the_facade_not_the_en.why_it_matters: !! An insulated лоджия wall does NOT mean the лоджия is inside the warm perimeter. It is not. Reading it the other way round would wrongly credit the лоджия with a thermal boundary it does not have, and the frost-free-without-heating target would look easier than it is.

two_level_model_2026_09_04.owner_insight: An opening does NOT divide a wall - the wall is one piece and is joined above the opening. His examples: G4c and G4e are one piece joined above the ванная door; the outer walls are continuous and joined above the window and door openings.
two_level_model_2026_09_04.the_rule_that_results: Combined with his earlier corner rule: SPLIT at a corner, or at a material / thickness change. DO NOT SPLIT at an opening. Openings stop being boundaries and become PROPERTIES OF A WALL.

MY_ERROR_CORRECTED.what: I split M1 from M7 and told the owner his own list was wrong. HE WAS RIGHT AND I WAS WRONG.
MY_ERROR_CORRECTED.why_I_got_it_wrong: I tested orientation by BOUNDING-BOX ASPECT RATIO. M7's box is 16 px wide by 38 tall, so it read as 'vertical'. A 16 px stub cannot express its own direction - the test was invalid for short pieces, and I applied it anyway and drew a confident conclusion from it.
MY_ERROR_CORRECTED.the_right_test: Whether two pieces share a BAND along the run axis. M1 y 740-775 and M7 y 743-781 share 32 px of band, so they are the same horizontal wall line. The 136 px gap between them is ~1480 mm - the лоджия door plus window unit, exactly as he said.
MY_ERROR_CORRECTED.lesson: !! A GEOMETRIC HEURISTIC MUST BE CHECKED AGAINST THE SIZE OF THE THING IT IS APPLIED TO. Aspect ratio is meaningless below a few times the wall thickness. And the owner knows his own flat - when his account and my raster measurement disagree, the measurement needs re-examining first, not his account.

O9_loggia_glazing_added.what: The owner: "we forgot about another opening... between M2 and M6b. It is full height and full length with no cladding, just window, big window from floor to ceiling."
O9_loggia_glazing_added.unique_property: !! IT IS THE ONLY OPENING IN THE FLAT WITH NO WALL ABOVE OR BELOW IT. So it has no head band and no sill band - the no-split-at-openings rule has nothing to apply to, because there is no wall there at all. Drawn DASHED for that reason.
O9_loggia_glazing_added.thermal_consequence: !!! AND IT CHANGES THE ЛОДЖИЯ SUM AGAIN, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The лоджия's ENTIRE south face is glass, floor to ceiling, facing DUE SOUTH. Solar gain is therefore at its theoretical maximum, which is the best possible case for the frost-free target. But heat loss through that face is also at its maximum, because there is no opaque wall in it at all - not even a sill band to store or resist. Combined with the earlier findings - nothing from the flat (MA is 300+70, R8 carries 150), nothing from the neighbour (M2 is cold-to-cold) - the target now rests ALMOST ENTIRELY ON THE GLAZING SPECIFICATION. It is a glass box on the warm side of the building. Anyone answering the frost-free question must treat the glazing as the whole of the design, not a component of it.

RETRACTION_basic_plan_does_not_omit_a_wa.what_I_recorded: Last round I recorded that the BASIC plan OMITS A WALL that the detailed plan draws, and wrote a caution into Apartment_Geometry_Sources telling future sessions to hunt for missing walls.
RETRACTION_basic_plan_does_not_omit_a_wa.the_test: Registered the basic plan onto the detailed plan using THICK-INK extent only, so labels and dimension strings could not bias it: x*0.7764+25, y*0.7751+5. Aspect mismatch 0.16% and all four corners land exactly. Then found every blob >=260 px where the detailed plan has ink and the registered basic plan does not, forgiving 4 px of slop.
RETRACTION_basic_plan_does_not_omit_a_wa.the_result: SIX blobs, and EVERY ONE IS A DIMENSION STRING - not a wall. The largest is the 710/250/2115/9.79 chain; the second is the 1050/3250/1490 vertical chain. There is NO wall-sized difference anywhere on the plan.
RETRACTION_basic_plan_does_not_omit_a_wa.so_the_truth_is: !! THE WALLS ARE THE SAME ON BOTH PLANS. What the basic plan lacks is the DIMENSIONS that let a reader see where one block ends and the next begins. That is why G1 read as ONE wall to me and as TWO blocks (250 + 120) to the owner - he was reading the dimensioned plan and I was reading the undimensioned one.
RETRACTION_basic_plan_does_not_omit_a_wa.lesson: !! The owner's instruction was right and my explanation of WHY was wrong. And the repo already said the thing that mattered - the detailed plan is "the only dimensioned source" - so the correct action was to USE it, not to invent a new failure mode. I generalised from one disagreement to a structural claim about the drawings, without testing it. The test took one script.

items.V2: 400 × 1140, MEASURED 2026-09-04, between R3 and R5 at the прихожая/кухня boundary. Long axis PERPENDICULAR to the façade.

three_ways_they_behave_unlike_walls: 1. IMMOVABLE - common property serving the whole riser. No layout variant may touch them.

2. They add surface INSIDE a room rather than bounding it. V1 stands in the туалет, so it has three finishable faces plus a top, and it REDUCES floor area while ADDING wall area - the opposite of how a wall behaves. !! That is exactly why the туалет has ~1.24 m² of usable floor rather than 1.8.
3. They cannot be chased or drilled, unlike the aerated block around them - so no service may cross them.
ventilation_shafts_as_a_class.consequence_for_quantities: A finish-area calculation that iterates walls only will UNDER-count. The shafts must be added as surface and subtracted as floor.

junction_correction_2026_09_04.WHY_IT_SLIPPED_and_the_rule: !! I placed that junction from the DETECTED red/green blob edges on his colour markup. A marker stroke is roughly 5 px wide at that scale, so a blob edge is good to about 50 mm - not to 5 mm. => BLOB EDGES LOCATE A WALL; THEY MUST NOT FIX A JUNCTION. Only a printed dimension may do that. Every junction placed the same way carries the same slop, so they are flagged for checking: G4C's two openings (derived from gaps, not printed at all), MA's O4a/O4b boundary, whether G6's O5 really starts AT R4, and where G4d's O6 begins.
junction_correction_2026_09_04.representation_added: Every wall is now drawn SOLID where material exists and DASHED across its openings, so both facts show at once: the wall is ONE piece, and the material stops at the opening. The dashed span over O8 lands on the printed 1 010 and the solid block beside it on the printed 710, which is a visual check anyone can repeat.

the_prihozhaya_kuhnya_divider.owner_insight: "We need to draw another line along V2 and up to R5, because it is a barrier... it is creating a structural divider. We have a ventilation shaft, we have a passway to the bigger room. So let's mark this space between V2 and R5 as another opening."
the_prihozhaya_kuhnya_divider.what_it_is: !! A DIVIDER PLANE THAT IS NOT A WALL. At basic x~658 it is composed of three different things in line: a 200 mm offset from the top wall (printed), the V2 ventilation shaft (1140 printed), the O10 passway (~958, NOT printed), and the R5 column (1050). No material spans it, so it is neither a wall nor a simple opening - it is a composed divider, and it is what separates the прихожая from the кухня/living zone.

O10_passway.how_measured: Off the raster at 12.61 mm per detailed px. !! That scale is confirmed TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS: from G8's printed 3250 over 332 basic px, and separately from V2's printed 1140, which measures back to 1135 (0.4% error). The printed 200 offset measures back to 214 (7%). So call the passway 950-1000 mm.
O10_passway.flanks: V2 (common-property ventilation shaft) on one side, R5 (monolithic RC frame column) on the other.
O10_passway.HARD_CONSTRAINT: !!! BOTH FLANKS ARE IMMOVABLE, SO THE PASSWAY CANNOT BE WIDENED - not by any layout, in any variant, at any budget. And it is the ONLY route from the прихожая into the кухня/living zone, so every person and every piece of furniture passes through ~958 mm.

consequences: The vault's corridor.min_clear_width rule is 1100 mm. This is ~958 - UNDER by about 140. That rule concerns CORRIDOR width rather than a zone-to-zone passway, so it is a FLAG and not a breach - but this is the narrowest point on the flat's main internal route and it is permanent.

!! Phase 2 puts the adults' bedroom BEYOND this passway. A Murphy bed, a sofa and a retractable glass divider all have to pass through ~958 mm. Worth checking each product's PACKED size before ordering, not after - and it connects to the vault's specify-large-and-cut finding, whose third motive is exactly access.
It also explains the прихожая's shape and its 9.79 m²: the hall is bounded on that side by a shaft plus a column rather than by a wall.

kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.finding: !!! THERE IS NO WALL between the кухня (5.24) and the living room (19.49). Verified on the detailed plan at 5x: the only things on that line are a DASHED zone boundary and a DASH-DOT grid axis. No hatching, no thickness, no jambs.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.consequence: In v0 the кухня is NOT A ROOM. It is a nominal ZONE inside one undivided 24.73 m² space, and the 5.24 / 19.49 split is the developer's AREA ACCOUNTING rather than a partition.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.what_it_invalidates: !! Two of the four arguments recorded earlier for v1's kitchen move are WITHDRAWN. The DAYLIGHT argument ("merging it into the living room is the only way that zone gets daylight") fails because they are already one space, so the zone already borrows the living room's window - badly, being at the far end from the glazing, but "no daylight" was wrong. The VENTILATION argument ("supply has no route without ducting") fails because a through-wall unit in the living room serves the whole open space.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.how_both_failed_the_same_way: !! I checked whether the KITCHEN had an external wall and never checked whether it was an ENCLOSED ROOM. A zone label on a plan is not a room, and I treated it as one for four rounds.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.what_survives: The owner's SEPARABILITY thesis, which was always the primary reason and depends on none of this; and the acoustics point about the middle room, which concerns a different room. But the review's claim of "three independent arguments" is now one.
kuhnya_is_a_zone_not_a_room.the_rule: !!! A LABEL ON A PLAN IS NOT A ROOM. The кухня had an area, a name, a printed dimension chain and fixtures drawn in it - everything a room has except walls. Before treating any labelled space as enclosed, CHECK ITS BOUNDARY FOR HATCHING.

closure_check.result: All eight room boundaries CLOSE once the кухня/living space is treated as one. No unaccounted gaps: every boundary segment is a wall, a shaft or a named opening.
closure_check.connectivity: !! THE FLAT IS A TREE, NOT A LOOP. Every room hangs off the прихожая and there is no second route between any two rooms, so the hall is a single point of failure for circulation and every inter-room trip passes through it. O10 is the ONLY edge into the largest space and is ~958 mm and unwidenable. And the лоджия is a LEAF BEHIND A LEAF, reached only through the 9.36 room - so from Phase 2 onward the household's only bulk storage sits behind a child's bedroom.
closure_check.verdict: Wall-segment stage COMPLETE structurally. Open dimensionally: lengths (10 of 25 printed), sill/head heights for O2 and O3, four blob-derived junctions, and the 2500 height datum.

plumbing_anchors.source: Owner marked them on _assets/wall_segments_v9_plumbing.png; isolated by pixel-diff against my own v9.

P1.note: !! THE FLAT'S ONLY WATER SOURCE. Immovable.

P2.serves: the kitchen now, and potentially a future laundry
P2.note: !! NO WATER at this point - kitchen water arrives from P1 UNDER THE FLOOR. Immovable.

plumbing_anchors.the_shape_of_it: TWO SEWERS but only ONE water source, and the kitchen water runs under the floor. So there are exactly TWO wet points in the flat, and any layout's wet fittings must attach to one of them.
plumbing_anchors.what_the_second_sewer_buys: !! The kitchen does NOT have to drain back to the туалет. That is genuine planning freedom and it is why a kitchen at that end of the flat works at all. ⚠ But DRAIN FALL caps how far a sink can sit from P2 - and the vault records drain fall as a first-order check that appeared in three consecutive rounds, including a developer layout that needed a 20 cm floor lift and a macerator.
plumbing_anchors.validates_v1_laundry: ✅ The owner said P2 could serve a future laundry. Checked against v1: its laundry label sits about 900 mm WEST of P2, so it is within reach. His remark and his own drawing agree.
plumbing_anchors.THE_COST_NOBODY_HAD_PRICED: !!! Kitchen water runs UNDER THE FLOOR, and the screed is ALREADY LAID with the heating pipes distributed in it. So MOVING A WET POINT MEANS BREAKING THE EXISTING SCREED, not just redrawing a plan. That belongs in the layout cost alongside demolishing the developer's partitions - and it is the same class as the vault's finding that a design error costs you the sanitaryware, not just the drawing.
plumbing_anchors.to_confirm: ⚠ The TOWEL HEATER is at P1, which is in the туалет - not in the ванная where towels are actually used. Worth confirming. If it is on the riser it is HYDRONIC, in which case the vault's electric-towel-rail flex-warranty finding does NOT apply here and the riser-recessing finding does instead.
